title: The telemetry that scaled a graph to zero
blurb: Wild values and double-counted retries poisoned rollups.
prompt: A dashboard metric collapsed to zero after one device sent a 64-bit overflow value, and retried batches doubled a fleet's totals because the store had no batch dedupe. The draft validates nothing before acking. Review it, fix it, and prove validation precedes acks and retries are batch-scoped.
aiNote: The draft acknowledges batches before validating, so out-of-range values and unknown devices are silently absorbed into aggregates that then look plausible, and on a partial store failure it re-sends the whole batch, double-counting the points that already landed.
testIdea: Send an out-of-range reading and assert the batch is rejected with the metric named; fail one sub-batch and assert only it is retried under the same batch id; query a 3-day range and assert 400.
followUps: How do you downsample without lying about peaks?
Where should per-device rate limits live, device or pipeline?
